builds.name: Reference: Ranked top core
builds.goal: Reference for Olaf: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ top players use most (3,808 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 58.5% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A relentless melee attacker who retrieves axes, fights at low health and keeps R active through contact. Attack uptime also recycles his true-damage swing. The current top provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Stridebreaker → Experimental Hexplate → Death's Dance. Conqueror keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Plated Steelcaps, Sterak's Gage, Spirit Visage.
builds.summary: The proven top baseline: Stridebreaker → Experimental Hexplate → Death's Dance, with Conqueror.
testPlan: Play it in top as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Stridebreaker → Experimental Hexplate → Death's Dance) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 58.5% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Stridebreaker → Experimental Hexplate → Death's Dance.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.
builds.author: Rift Build Lab ranked data

kitEvidence.formula:
Passive: Olaf gains [10 / 15 / 20] Armor and [10 / 15 / 20] Magic Resist.

Active: Olaf cleanses all Immobilizing and Disabling effects on himself and becomes immune to them for [3] seconds. While active, Olaf gains [10 / 20 / 30 + (0.25) × AD] Attack Damage. Hitting a champion with an Attack or Reckless Swing extends the duration by [2.5] seconds.

Additionally, Olaf gains [(0.2 / 0.45 / 0.7) × 100]% Move Speed towards enemy champions for [1] second.

Olaf ferociously swings his axes, dealing [70 / 115 / 160 / 205 / 250 + (0.5) × AD] true damage. If the enemy dies, the cost is refunded.

Attacks lower the Cooldown of this Ability by 1 second, increased to 2 seconds when attacking monsters.

Olaf throws an axe, dealing [70 / 120 / 170 / 220 / 270 + (1) × AD[statFormula=2]] physical damage and Slowing by [(0.3 / 0.35 / 0.4 / 0.45 / 0.5) × 100]% for up to [3] seconds (based on distance travelled). Champions hit lose [20]% Armor for [4] seconds.

If Olaf picks up the axe, this Ability's Cooldown is reduced to [(2.5) × (runtimeCooldownMultiplier)] seconds, or fully refunded if [(2.5) × (runtimeCooldownMultiplier)] seconds has elapsed.

Olaf gains [(0.4 / 0.5 / 0.6 / 0.7 / 0.8) × 100]% Attack Speed for [5] seconds, and [10 / 40 / 70 / 100 / 130] plus [17.5]% missing Health Shield (up to a maximum of [10 / 40 / 70 / 100 / 130 + ((0.175) × ((1 + (-1) × (0.3)))) × Stat(12)] Shield below [30]% Health) for [2.5] seconds.
Olaf gains up to [characterLevelInterpolation(0.5 → 1; raw flags preserved)] Attack Speed and [characterLevelInterpolation(0.08 → 0.25; raw flags preserved)] Life Steal, based on his missing Health.

builds.name: Low-health Bloodmail swing
builds.summary: Test low-health bloodmail swing against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test low-health bloodmail swing against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Berserker Rage gains attack speed/lifesteal with missing health, while Bloodmail gains AD as health falls; Reckless Swing adds 0.5 total AD true damage and attacks refund its cooldown. Visage supports lifesteal and Tough It Out's missing-health shield during Ragnarok contact.
testPlan: Required state: Reach low health safely with R ready and champion attacks connected.
Compare E casts and healing at fixed low-health percentages.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Execution burst kills him before sustain, or kiting ends Ragnarok.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Low health is a controlled test condition, not free permanent maximum Bloodmail value.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Overlord's Bloodmail, Blade of The Ruined King, Sterak's Gage, Spirit Visage, Black Cleaver, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Physical matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Olaf: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A relentless melee attacker who retrieves axes, fights at low health and keeps R active through contact. Attack uptime also recycles his true-damage swing. Fix current health, axe retrieval and R uptime. Compare low-health attack pressure with surviving real damage; CC immunity does not mean damage immunity. Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
builds.summary: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows.
testPlan: Kit question for Olaf: Fix current health, axe retrieval and R uptime. Compare low-health attack pressure with surviving real damage; CC immunity does not mean damage immunity.

Start with the early core (Stridebreaker, then matchup armor) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: Armor and access may turn survival into additional attack/spell windows. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Olaf throws an axe into the ground at a target location, dealing damage to enemies it passes through and reducing their Armor and Move Speed. If Olaf picks up the axe, the ability's cooldown is reset. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
The route fails Olaf's stated kit question: Fix current health, axe retrieval and R uptime. Compare low-health attack pressure with surviving real damage; CC immunity does not mean damage immunity.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: Randuin is conditional on the enemy attack/crit profile; it costs an offensive slot.
Full cost 16,100 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Stridebreaker, then matchup armor. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Randuin's Omen, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.name: Axe Spellblade caster
builds.summary: Test axe spellblade caster against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.goal: Test axe spellblade caster against conventional damage at equal gold.
builds.hypothesis: Picking up Undertow caps its cooldown at the documented short interval; Trinity rewards an attack between axe throws while Shojin supports Q/E repetition. Cleaver accompanies Q's armor removal, but Reckless Swing remains true damage and does not benefit armor penetration.
testPlan: Required state: Retrieve axes without abandoning champion contact.
Count Q and E casts with safe versus obstructed pickups.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Bad axe placement makes the build's haste and Spellblade rhythm inaccessible.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: Armor reduction does not increase E true damage or make axe cooldown literally zero on every pickup.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
